channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Armenian PM threatens resignation over proposed constitutional referendum
item.description: Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan has vowed to resign if a proposed constitutional referendum fails to gain majority support, and will not seek re-election if it succeeds. The new constitution is central to his "Real Armenia" program and could facilitate a peace agreement with Azerbaijan by removing constitutional clauses questioning Azerbaijan's sovereignty over Nagorno-Karabakh.

item.title: Tajikistan's Ministry of Energy Comments on Collapse of Uzbek Power Line Support
item.description: A support tower for the 500 kV high-voltage power line L-503 collapsed in Tajikistan's Zafarabad district due to strong winds. The Ministry of Energy and Water Resources stated this did not affect Tajikistan's power supply as the line is not used by its energy system. The incident caused power outages in parts of Uzbekistan.

item.title: Uzbek President Meets with Head of International Judo Federation
item.description: The President of Uzbekistan met with the head of the International Judo Federation to discuss expanding cooperation in developing the national judo school and training young athletes. The meeting focused on strengthening the partnership between the federation and Uzbekistan's sports institutions.

item.title: Uzbekistan Signs Agreement on Youth Employment and Safe Migration
item.description: Uzbekistan has signed a trilateral memorandum of cooperation aimed at training youth in in-demand professions and foreign languages, and facilitating their employment in the international labor market. The agreement, part of the '2+6' program, will streamline efforts in subsidizing language learning, vocational training, and legal labor migration.

item.title: Xi Jinping: China-Russia-US Trilateral Meeting Will Yield Significant Future Results
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping stated that the first trilateral meeting between China, Russia, and the United States in Shenzhen will produce significant future results. He emphasized the need for strengthened cooperation to overcome global challenges, suggesting that shared interests can foster peace and mutual benefit.

item.title: International Court of Justice Rules Myanmar Committed Genocide Against Rohingya
item.description: The International Court of Justice has ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya Muslim minority. The court ordered safe return and reparations for refugees. This is the first time in the court's 80-year history that it has found a country guilty of genocide, citing systematic destruction and violence.

item.title: Navoiy Region Enterprises to Develop Using German Technologies
item.description: Cooperation is being established in the Navoiy region to enhance the technological capabilities of industrial enterprises, localize component production for the automotive industry, and facilitate market access to Europe. A memorandum signed with the Ministry of Economy and Finance aims to adapt local businesses to European standards and explore innovation institute creation.

item.title: British Library Manuscripts on Display in Tajikistan's Khujand Fortress Museum
item.description: Copies of 18 classical Persian-Tajik literature manuscripts from the British Library are exhibited at the Khujand Fortress Museum in Tajikistan. The exhibition, running until January 2027, marks 35 years of UK-Tajikistan diplomatic ties and 25 years of the British embassy in Dushanbe. It showcases works by Rudaki, Firdawsi, Omar Khayyam, and Kamoli Khujandi.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Turkey Identify New Priorities for Economic Cooperation
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with Turkish Vice President Cevdet Yılmaz to discuss boosting economic ties. The meeting, part of the first Uzbek-Turkish High-Level Business Support Council, highlighted strong interest in expanding partnership. Uzbekistan's economy has tripled since 2017, attracting significant foreign investment, with Turkey noted as a key strategic partner.

item.title: Former Head of Interior Ministry's Drug Control Committee Sentenced
item.description: A court in Astana has issued a sentence for Daniyar Meirkhan, former chairman of the Interior Ministry's Drug Control Committee. He was found guilty of forcing sexual acts and fined 6.487 million tenge. The case was heard in a closed session, and the verdict has not yet entered into legal force.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Turkey Expand Cooperation in Geology and Mining
item.description: Uzbekistan and Turkey are strengthening their partnership in the geology and mining sectors. Uzbek Minister of Mining and Geology Bobur Islamov held talks with delegations from Turkish companies "ESAN" and "Eksim Holding." Discussions focused on joint projects, attracting foreign investment, and implementing innovative technologies.

item.title: Brazilian Woman Faces Severe Penalties for Drug Smuggling on Bali
item.description: A Brazilian woman was arrested on the Indonesian island of Bali for suspected drug smuggling. Authorities found over 3.6 kg of liquid cocaine hidden in personal hygiene products in her luggage. She faces a potential life sentence.

item.title: Uzbek Riders Secure Top Places in Eurasian League World Cup
item.description: Uzbekistan's equestrian team achieved notable success at the Eurasian League World Cup finals in Astana. Alisherjon Erkinov secured first place in the 125 cm competition, followed by A'zam Tolibboev in second. A rider from Kyrgyzstan took third.

item.title: Afghan UN Envoy Advocates for Women's Rights and Public Participation in Afghanistan's Future
item.description: Afghanistan's UN Representative, Nasir Ahmad Faiq, urged support for citizens' rights, education, and employment for women and girls. He emphasized public participation in shaping the country's future and pledged to convey the Afghan people's voices globally, striving for an independent and peaceful Afghanistan.

item.title: Group Arrested in Karakalpakstan for Allegedly Embezzling 1 Billion Som via Malicious APK Files
item.description: A group has been apprehended in Karakalpakstan on suspicion of embezzling approximately 1 billion Uzbek soums using malicious APK files. Investigators discovered data from 162 bank cards in the suspects' Telegram communications. The stolen funds were reportedly used to purchase expensive phones and fund betting accounts.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Eco-Police Finds Violations in Air Pollution Control at Tashkent Plant
item.description: Uzbekistan's eco-police discovered violations of air pollution control measures at an ООО "R.P." plant in Tashkent. The facility, producing polyethylene granules, failed to implement atmospheric protection measures, conduct emissions monitoring, or install necessary gas cleaning equipment. Air samples showed elevated levels of nitrogen dioxide and dust.

item.title: UN Official: ISIS-K in Afghanistan Possesses Armed Drones, Increasing Pressure on Kabul
item.description: Terrorist groups in Afghanistan, particularly ISIS-K, possess armed drones and are using them to pressure Kabul, according to the Acting Under-Secretary-General of the UN Office of Counter-Terrorism. Alexandre Zouev stated that ISIS-K is rebuilding its capabilities with modern equipment, including drones, for operations within and beyond Afghanistan.

item.title: Kazakhstan Urges Practical International Engagement with Afghanistan
item.description: Kazakhstan has called for practical international engagement with Afghanistan. This initiative aims to foster cooperation and address regional dynamics. The call comes amidst ongoing discussions about Afghanistan's role in international forums and its relations with neighboring countries.

item.title: Putin: Ukraine Must Accept 'Compromises' for Peace, Crimea Bridge Attack Response 'Painful'
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin stated that Ukraine should agree to 'compromises' proposed by the US to end the conflict. He emphasized Russia's interest in stopping the war and suggested that Ukraine should accept the proposed compromises, which he claimed Russia has already agreed to.

item.title: Uzbek President Urges Turkish Companies to Participate in Major Projects
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev called on Turkish investors to actively participate in the construction of New Tashkent and major infrastructure projects. Cooperation in agriculture, including organic fertilizers and water-saving technologies, was also discussed. The president encouraged Turkish firms to build residential complexes, commercial centers, and hotels in the new city.

item.title: Non-existent Presidential Candidate Appears in Kyrgyzstan's Information System
item.description: A 'ghost' candidate, Solpiev Aybek Melisovich, appeared in Kyrgyzstan's 'Tunduk' app for collecting presidential candidate signatures. The Central Election Commission stated it was a technical error during infrastructure testing, where a test record was mistakenly displayed. The error was quickly fixed and did not affect real data.

item.title: Iran Conflict Reshapes Global Energy System, States International Energy Agency
item.description: The conflict in Iran is altering the global energy system, prompting countries to abandon imported fuels and focus on local energy and electrification due to potential disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz. The International Energy Agency predicts the world market will not return to pre-war levels.

item.title: Central Asian Nations Preparing Unified Platform for Electricity Trading
item.description: Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, and Tajikistan are preparing to launch a unified electricity market. The 'Energia' Coordination and Dispatch Center is seeking a company to create and manage a trading platform. The project, supported by the World Bank, aims to facilitate cross-border electricity trade, with initial transactions expected by late 2028 or early 2029.

item.title: Trilateral Meeting of Trump, Putin, and Xi Concludes in China
item.description: A trilateral meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin concluded in China on the sidelines of the APEC summit. The leaders discussed global stability, nuclear non-proliferation, and the conflict in Ukraine during the 90-minute meeting.

item.title: Afghan Women Activists Discuss Challenges with UN Representative in Kabul
item.description: Afghan women activists met with UN Special Representative Rabab Fatima in Kabul to discuss challenges facing women and girls. They called for greater opportunities and meaningful participation in society, emphasizing the need for women to be active participants in decision-making processes affecting their lives.

item.title: Uzbekistan Citizens Invited to Work in Croatia with 1000 Euro Salary
item.description: Uzbek citizens are being invited to work in Croatia, with job offers for construction specialists. The advertised salary is 1000 euros per month. The employer provides free accommodation and a monthly compensation of 80 euros for food expenses.

item.title: 831 Kazakh Citizens Opt Out of Social Payments Via Digital Service
item.description: Since its launch in October, 831 Kazakh citizens have used the digital service to voluntarily waive social payments. This service allows state support to be prioritized for those genuinely in need. The option is available online through the eGov Mobile app and the eGov.kz portal.

item.title: Paris City Council Votes to Grant Honorary Citizenship to Afghan Women and Girls
item.description: The Paris City Council has voted to grant the title of “Honorary Citizen of Paris” to Afghan women and girls. This decision aims to support them and highlights their struggle against gender-based restrictions. Council members also called for gender apartheid in Afghanistan to be recognized.

item.title: Saida Mirziyoyeva Outlines Priorities for New Uzbek-Turkish Business Council
item.description: Saida Mirziyoyeva stated her intention to focus on strengthening investment and business ties, removing barriers for entrepreneurs, and supporting projects as co-chair of the Uzbek side of the new Uzbek-Turkish Council. The first meeting included Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and Turkish Vice President Cevdet Yılmaz.

item.title: Uzbek Minister: Afghanistan Has Right to Amudarya Water Amid QoshTepa Canal Construction
item.description: Uzbekistan's Water Resources Minister stated that Afghanistan has a right to Amudarya water, emphasizing ongoing dialogue with the Taliban regarding the QoshTepa canal. The minister indicated that an interstate agreement on water distribution is anticipated upon the canal's completion, a process expected to take many years.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Introduces 'Tunduk' App for Presidential Candidate Support Collection
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is utilizing the 'Tunduk' mobile application for collecting support signatures for presidential candidates. This digital process, approved by the Central Election Commission, simplifies the previous paper-based method, saving time and resources. The head of the CEC's IT department explained the system's convenience for citizens and candidates.

item.title: Over Half of Uzbek Teachers Failed Professional Certification in Last Two Years
item.description: In Uzbekistan, 62.3% of teachers failed professional certification tests over the past two years, according to the National Agency for Quality Assurance in Education. Out of 47,936 participating teachers, only 3.4% achieved the highest scores. Graduates of classical state universities had the highest pass rate at 39.9%.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Turkmenistan Sign Energy Cooperation Agreement in Ashgabat
item.description: The 7th session of the Kyrgyz-Turkmen intergovernmental commission on trade, economic, scientific, technical, and humanitarian cooperation was held in Ashgabat. Key discussions focused on expanding trade, economic, and energy partnerships, as well as transport and logistics. An agreement was signed between the National Electric Network of Kyrgyzstan and Turkmenistan Energy Corporation.

item.title: Russia Attacks Kyiv Shortly After Summits with US and China
item.description: Russia launched an attack on Kyiv shortly after summits involving the US and China. The attack resulted in the death of a 26-year-old man and injured at least four others. One drone reportedly hit a building near the Netherlands embassy.

item.title: Astana identifies over 150 violations in food price control since early 2026
item.description: Astana's price control commission has detected more than 150 violations in monitoring food prices since the beginning of 2026. The city's trade and consumer rights protection department is actively monitoring prices in various stores and markets, ensuring adherence to the 15% markup limit on socially significant food products.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan Plan to Resume Flights and Simplify Visa Regime
item.description: Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan are planning to resume air travel and simplify the visa regime, according to the Uzbek Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Discussions included transport links, border crossings, and visa-free travel for residents of border areas. Regular flights between Tashkent and Ashgabat were also considered, along with consular protection.

item.title: Uzbek Professor Sentenced to 10 Years for Espionage in Kazakhstan
item.description: An Uzbek international relations professor, Dr. Ikboljon Qoraboyev, has reportedly received a 10-year prison sentence for espionage following a closed-door trial in Kazakhstan. Detained in July, his case has been shrouded in mystery, with neither Kazakh nor Uzbek officials commenting. Relatives stated he was charged under Article 176 of Kazakhstan's Criminal Code for collecting state secrets.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Implement Drug Testing for Government Officials
item.description: Kazakhstan has approved new rules for drug and psychotropic substance testing of civil servants, effective November 29. The rules outline observation of employee behavior by HR and supervisors, with specific signs like sudden behavioral changes or impaired coordination potentially leading to medical examination. Refusal to test will be documented.

item.title: WHO Reports Decline in Respiratory Infections and Measles Cases in Afghanistan
item.description: The World Health Organization (WHO) reported a decrease in acute respiratory infections and measles cases in Afghanistan during October. Respiratory infections saw a 3.8 percent decline, with 94,104 cases and 149 deaths recorded. Suspected measles cases dropped by 22.6 percent, with 1,152 cases and five related deaths reported.

item.title: Kazakhstan's People's Council Discusses 25 Initiatives for Workers' Rights and Labor Relations
item.description: The People's Council of Kazakhstan, with support from the Pavlodar regional administration, held a meeting with representatives of the trade union movement. Discussions focused on social-labor policy, protecting workers' rights, and developing labor relations. The meeting resulted in 25 initiatives proposed to the People's Council to protect workers' interests and develop systemic solutions at the national level.
